sources.title: UN peacekeeping mission in Western Sahara to expire amid US, Russia vetoes
Rival US and Russian resolutions on Western Sahara fail at UN

en.title: US and Russia veto UN resolutions to extend Western Sahara mission
en.dek: Both powers blocked proposals, leaving the UN mission MINURSO set to expire.
facts: The UN mission MINURSO was established in 1991 to oversee a ceasefire and prepare a referendum in Western Sahara.
The United States drafted a resolution to extend the mission for one year, remove the word "referendum" from its name, and base negotiations solely on Morocco's autonomy plan.
Russia vetoed the US draft, describing it as a unilateral approach.
The United States vetoed a Russian draft that would have renewed the mission unchanged.
The mission's mandate expires on Saturday unless the council adopts a new resolution.
body: The United Nations mission MINURSO, which monitors a ceasefire in Western Sahara, is due to expire on Saturday unless the council adopts a new resolution. The Security Council rejected both the United States and Russia's proposals to extend the mission. Eleven of the fifteen members voted in favor of the US draft, while three abstained.

The United States drafted a resolution that would have extended MINURSO for one year, removed the word "referendum" from the mission's name, and limited negotiations to Morocco's autonomy plan. Russia vetoed the draft, describing it as a unilateral approach. The US representative, Michael Waltz, said the referendum had stalled for decades. The US also vetoed a Russian draft that would have kept the mission unchanged.

Russia's draft proposed renewing the existing mission without changes to its mandate, but it failed to secure the nine votes needed for adoption. Nebenzia said the council must not give a blessing to a one-sided approach.

Morocco's royal palace welcomed the failure to renew MINURSO, stating that the issue should be removed from the Security Council's agenda. The Polisario Front's representative, Sidi Omar, thanked Russia for vetoing the US resolution, saying it would have undermined Sahrawi self‑determination. The UN mission has not held a referendum for decades. Low‑level fighting has continued since the Polisario resumed armed struggle in 2020.
en.context: MINURSO was created in 1991 to monitor a ceasefire and prepare a referendum in Western Sahara, a former Spanish colony claimed by Morocco and the Algeria‑backed Polisario Front. Disagreements over who could vote have prevented a referendum from taking place.
